extraction.name: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, V éronique Zimpfer, and Éric Bavu
extraction.publisher: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam), French-German Research Institute of Saint-Louis (ISL)
extraction.citeAs: J. Hauret, M. Olivier, C. Langrenne, S. Poirée, and É. Bavu, “vibravox (revision 071945b),” 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected through a rigorous data collection process involving 200 participants (188 retained after post-processing). Participants wore five different body-conduction audio sensors and an airborne reference microphone. The recording protocol consisted of four steps: speech-clean (reading sentences), speechless-noisy (silence in noisy environment), speechless-clean (silence in quiet environment), and speech-noisy (speaking in noisy environment). Noise was spatialized using a 3D ambisonics spatializer with 56 loudspeakers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: A total of 30,568 sentences were initially collected from 200 participants. Post-processing filters removed utterances with obvious deficiencies such as mispronunciations, sensor shifting, or malfunctions. This resulted in the retention of 188 participants and 28,471 sentences, excluding 6% of participants and 6.8% of pronounced sentences.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Audio recordings from five body-conduction sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, one laryngophone) and one airborne reference microphone (Shure WH20XLR). Textual data originated from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A 20 Hz high-pass filter was uniformly applied to each acquisition channel. Textual data was filtered to exclude proper names (except common first names, town/region/country names), numbers, Greek letters, mathematical symbols, and syntactic errors. Text normalization included lowercasing and removing punctuation except apostrophes. Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the CoML lab text phonemizer, with manual correction for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Post-processing involved automatic filtering based on indicators extracted using the whisper-timestamped model. Filters removed samples with Phoneme Error Rate (PER) > 10%, low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR < 1.5 dB), or sensitivity drift (Lspeech_50 < Lsilence_50). Voice Activity Detection (VAD) timestamps were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides to eliminate edge artifacts. The dataset was split by speaker into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% test sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Linguistic transcriptions were created from French Wikipedia text. Phonetic transcriptions were generated using the CoML lab text phonemizer and manually corrected for unrecognized words. Recording conditions were annotated as part of the dataset structure (speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, speechless-noisy).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: whisper-timestamped model, CoML lab text phonemizer
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available on HuggingFace. It is versioned (revision 071945b). No specific future update or deprecation policy is mentioned.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Audio recordings of speech and physiological sounds (heart rate, breathing) from 188 participants. Demographic information includes gender (97 Female, 91 Male) and age (Mean 28.55 years, range 18-82).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance research in body-conduction audio sensors for robust communication in noisy environments, with potential applications in military, industrial, and wearable technology contexts. It addresses the lack of French-language BCM datasets and diverse sensor types.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to French language speakers. The participants were recruited to be gender-balanced, but the age range is 18-82. The sensors used are specific types of body-conduction microphones, which may not represent all possible sensor technologies.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing BCM datasets often lack scale and diversity. Vibravox addresses this but is limited to French. Some sensors (e.g., temple vibration pickup) have limited bandwidth. In-ear microphones may have acoustic sealing issues for some ear canal anatomies. The dataset does not include synthetic data generation for training, relying on real data.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of deep learning models for speech enhancement (bandwidth extension), speech recognition (speech-to-phonemes), and speaker verification. It can also be used for analyzing sensor characteristics and physiological sound monitoring.
